name: Bezalel
overview: Bezalel was a male craftsman from the tribe of Judah who was divinely appointed by God to oversee the construction of the tabernacle. His unique calling highlights his special role in the sacred task of building the dwelling place for God's presence among the Israelites. He is noted specifically for his craftsmanship in this important work.
namesAndTitles: The name Bezalel means 'in the shadow of God [El],' reflecting a close association with divine protection and guidance. This proper name underscores his God-ordained role in the tabernacle's construction as recorded in Exodus 31:2.
familyAndRelationships: Bezalel is identified in Scripture as the son of Uri, establishing his family lineage within the tribe of Judah. Beyond this, Scripture does not record additional family relationships for him.
scriptureSignificance: Bezalel's significance lies in his God-given ability and appointment to build the tabernacle, a central element of Israel's worship and God's covenant presence. His role exemplifies how God equips and calls individuals for specific purposes in His redemptive plan. Through Bezalel's skilled craftsmanship, the tabernacle was constructed according to divine instructions, enabling Israel to worship God properly.
